sections.h2: Where is Dothan, Alabama, and why does it cover three counties?
sections.html:
Dothan is the county seat of Houston County in the southeast corner of Alabama, about 20 miles west of the Georgia line and 16 miles north of Florida. The city limits also reach north into Henry County and northwest into Dale County, which makes parcel location a real question for sellers.

It is Alabama's eighth-largest city, with 71,072 residents at the 2020 census, and it covers roughly 90 square miles. The terrain is flat and forested, part of the Wiregrass region, and the city is the commercial hub for southeast Alabama, southwest Georgia and part of the Florida Panhandle.

sections.h2: How did Dothan grow from a peanut town?
sections.html:
Dothan's early settlement was called Poplar Head, after a spring, and residents voted to incorporate on November 11, 1885, taking the name Dothan on a clergyman's suggestion. A railroad stop arrived in 1893, which gave farmers a way to ship produce, and timber and cotton followed.

The boll weevil wrecked cotton in the early 1900s, and farmers switched to peanuts. About one quarter of the U.S. peanut crop is now grown within 75 miles of the city, and Dothan calls itself the Peanut Capital of the World. The National Peanut Festival, held each November, draws up to 200,000 visitors.

Dothan became the Houston County seat on May 9, 1903. The regional airport opened in 1965, Troy University started a Dothan campus in 1961, and Wallace Community College was founded in 1969.

sections.h2: How has Dothan's population changed over time?
sections.html:
Dothan has grown in every census since 1890, though the pace has slowed. The city counted 48,750 people in 1980, 57,737 in 2000, 65,496 in 2010 and 71,072 in 2020.

About 19.3 percent of residents in 2020 were 65 or older, and nearly a third of households were one person living alone. Many of those homes will change hands in the next decade as owners downsize, move to family or pass away, and heirs often prefer a quick sale over managing a vacant house from far away.

sections.h2: What are the biggest employers in Dothan?
sections.html:
Health care, schools and a nuclear plant lead the list. Southeast Alabama Medical Center is the largest employer, followed by the Dothan and Houston County school systems and Flowers Hospital.

The city's 2011 financial report, which is the list Wikipedia reproduces, put the top ten as follows:

  • Southeast Alabama Medical Center, 2,500 employees
  • Dothan City and Houston County Schools, 1,973
  • Flowers Hospital, 1,100
  • City of Dothan, 927
  • Southern Nuclear (Farley plant), 860
  • Perdue Farms, 800
  • Michelin, 542

Those counts are more than a decade old, so treat them as a picture of which kinds of employers anchor the area rather than current payroll numbers. Sony closed its Dothan plant in 2010, and Pemco Aviation closed its facility in 2012. Sellers who lived through those closings know how a single employer can change a street's resale picture.

sections.h2: What does the weather mean for a Dothan house?
sections.html:
Dothan has hot, humid summers and mild winters, and rain falls all year, with August the wettest month at 6.17 inches on average. Snow is rare, though a significant event hit the city on January 21, 2025.

Tornadoes are a recurring concern in spring, summer and fall. Wikipedia, citing a risk index, says Dothan's tornado activity runs below the Alabama average but 79 percent above the national average.

  • Check roof condition and shingle age, since tornado and thunderstorm wind are a regular worry here.
  • Look for moisture under floors and in crawlspaces after heavy summer rain.
  • Keep records of any storm repairs and insurance claims for the buyer's agent or your closing agent.

The terrain is generally flat, with small hills sloping toward the Chattahoochee River to the east and the Gulf coastal plain to the south.

sections.h2: How do you get around Dothan, and does it affect value?
sections.html:
Dothan is ringed by Ross Clark Circle (State Route 210), a bypass that carries U.S. 84 on the north, U.S. 231 on the west and U.S. 431 on the east. Where a house sits relative to the Circle is a simple way to describe its location to a buyer.

The city has no interstate. The nearest, I-10, runs about 32 miles to the south, and Dothan is the only top-ten Alabama city without interstate access. U.S. 84 goes east 55 miles to Bainbridge, Georgia, and U.S. 231 goes south 83 miles to Panama City, Florida.

Dothan Regional Airport has Delta service, and the Wiregrass Transit Authority offers dial-a-ride rather than fixed routes. Most households here rely on cars, so a driveway, garage and distance to the Circle all get weighed.

sections.h2: Who holds the schools, and what else do buyers look at?
sections.html:
Most children in Dothan attend Dothan City Schools or Houston County Schools, and private options include Houston Academy, Providence Christian School, Northside Methodist Academy, Emmanuel Christian School and Westgate Christian School. Higher education includes Troy University's Dothan campus, Wallace Community College, Fortis College and the Alabama College of Osteopathic Medicine.

The city uses a mayor and a six-district board of commissioners, with a city manager running daily operations. Because ordinances and permits come from the city, a seller with unpermitted work should ask city staff what is required before listing.

sections.h2: How does a Dothan home sale close?
sections.html:
A sale closes when the deed is recorded with the probate office of the county where the parcel sits, and Alabama collects a recordation tax at that time. Alabama Code section 40-22-1 sets the tax at 50 cents per $500 of value, and a form stating the actual purchase price goes with the deed.

Because Dothan reaches into three counties, ask your closing agent to confirm the county before anything is signed. Most parcels are in Houston County, but a few are not.

Property tax in Alabama is due October 1 and delinquent after December 31, per the Alabama Department of Revenue. A sale that closes in the fourth quarter should settle that bill on the closing statement.

sections.h2: What do Dothan sellers usually face?
sections.html:
Many sellers in Dothan are managing an older house, an inheritance or a rental that has run its course. Others are leaving for work and cannot wait through months of showings.

  • Heirs spread across states who inherit a Dothan house they do not want to manage.
  • Landlords with units that need more work than the rent supports.
  • Owners with roof, plumbing or HVAC problems after years of deferral.
  • Sellers with timing pressure from a job move or a divorce.

A direct cash sale can take away showings, lender appraisals and repair requests. If you want to see what that looks like for your house, submit the form on this page.

faqs.q: How many people live in Dothan?
faqs.a: Dothan had 71,072 residents at the 2020 census, making it the eighth-largest city in Alabama.
Dothan is the county seat of Houston County, and parts of the city extend into Dale and Henry counties. Confirm your parcel's county before you record a deed.
No. The nearest interstate is I-10, about 32 miles south. Dothan is served by U.S. 84, 231 and 431, which meet at Ross Clark Circle.

faqs.q: When are Dothan property taxes due?
faqs.a: Alabama property tax is due October 1 and is delinquent after December 31, according to the state revenue department.

faqs.q: What tax do I pay to record a deed in Dothan?
faqs.a: Alabama's recordation tax is 50 cents per $500 of value on the deed, paid to the probate office before recording. Your closing agent normally handles it.
